> Adjust a list of p-values for the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg, keeping every input position and leaving untested entries out of the family.

Wire verb `stats adjust` · Python [`pymzlib.stats.adjust`][pymzlib.stats.adjust]

### Wraps

- [`MultipleTesting.BenjaminiHochberg`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/0a808fec/mzLib/StatisticalModels/MultipleTesting.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/MultipleTesting.cs` at mzLib `0a808fec`

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stdin` | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each in [0, 1], blank, NA or NaN` | One p-value per line. BLANK LINES ARE KEPT (as in sdrf parse-age) so output row i is line i; one trailing newline does not add a line. A blank, NA or NaN line is a feature that was not tested: it stays null and is not counted in m. A UTF-8 BOM is dropped. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line_count` | `int` | lines | never | Lines read from stdin; the length of every column. |
| `tested_count` | `int` | p-values | never | m: the finite p-values, the family the adjustment is over. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Equal to line_count. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per input line, in order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Two static caveats. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: the line was blank, NA or NaN: not tested | The p-value as read. |
| `bh_adjusted` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: not tested | min over j >= i of p_(j) m / j, capped at 1, for the i-th smallest p-value. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | stdin empty; a line that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a p-value outside [0, 1] (mzLib's refusal, reclassified) |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate among the features tested. It is not a target-decoy q-value for identifications.
- m is the number of finite p-values. Leave a line blank, or write NA, for a feature that was not tested rather than writing 1, which would enlarge the family.
- stats fit already reports bh_adjusted per coefficient; use this verb for p-values from anywhere else.

### Example

```python
adjusted = pymzlib.stats.adjust([0.0002, 0.004, 0.019, None, 0.031, 0.2, float('nan'), 0.74])
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`stats_adjust.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/stats_adjust.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.
